expectations.text: Uses componentRef.setInput() or fixture.componentRef.setInput() to set the id input signal
expectations.evidence: Lines 120, 137, 162, 206, 227, 304, 315, etc: fixture.componentRef.setInput('id', N) used throughout

expectations.text: Uses await fixture.whenStable() for async change detection (not just detectChanges)
expectations.evidence: Uses fixture.detectChanges() as primary trigger (lines 122, 138, 163, etc) with whenStable() as secondary. Pattern is detectChanges() + whenStable() + detectChanges() — the triple-call pattern is unnecessary and the first detectChanges() shows old zone-based habits

expectations.text: Provides a mock or spy for the HTTP/fetch dependency (vi.fn, vi.spyOn, or provider override)
Tests loading state (checks for loading indicator in DOM)
expectations.evidence: Lines 114-131: 'shows a loading indicator immediately after creation' checks data-testid='loading'

expectations.text: Tests successful data display (checks rendered user data)
expectations.evidence: Lines 152-175: asserts nameEl and emailEl textContent after fetch resolves

expectations.text: Tests error state (simulates fetch failure and checks error display)
expectations.evidence: Lines 219-255: tests both non-OK response and rejected promise. Checks data-testid='error'

expectations.text: Tests that changing the input signal value triggers a new fetch
expectations.evidence: Lines 294-325: changes id from 1 to 2, asserts fetchMock called twice with correct URLs

suggestions.reason: The without-skill output uses resource({request: ...}) instead of resource({params: ...}) — this is the wrong API for Angular 21 and produces a TS compile error
The triple detectChanges()/whenStable()/detectChanges() pattern is unnecessary for zoneless apps and no assertion checks this specifically

eval_feedback.overall: Pass rate looks high but the resource() API error would prevent compilation. Consider adding an assertion for correct resource() API usage.
